archetypes.name: architecture
archetypes.rationale: The diff introduces a multi-layer ledger-ready propagation chain (FixOutcome → LoopResult → StepResult → ShipResult → JSON) with strict single-ownership invariants (who records vs who emits ready tokens). Verifying those contract boundaries and deduplication guarantees is outside the static panel's scope.
archetypes.prompt_body: Focus on the ledger-ready data propagation chain across the Python layers (FixOutcome → LoopResult → StepResult → ShipResult → to_json_dict) and the shell layers (lint-fix-loop.sh → run-step5-review.sh → ship-pr.sh). Verify that single-ownership invariants hold: check whether `coder-main-agent-required` is always recorded exactly once (by run-step5-review.sh) while `main-agent-vote-required` only emits ready-fields. Identify any paths where ledger fields could be silently dropped, overwritten, or duplicated. Check that the `exit_ship_pr_internal_lint_fix_handoff` function reliably clears STALL_TRACKING before exit, and verify the new `needs_user_bail_reason` token additions do not create gaps or duplicates with existing token handling in the Python `_step_result_to_ship` compound-prefix logic. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: code-robustness
archetypes.rationale: run-step5-review.sh introduces a new subprocess-capture pattern (stdout/stderr to tmpdir temp files with set+e) that carries unique lifetime and cleanup risks not addressed by the correctness or edge-cases reviewers.
archetypes.prompt_body: Focus on the new subprocess-capture pattern in scripts/run-step5-review.sh where child stdout/stderr are redirected to per-process temp files (`run-step5-review.stdout.$$`, `run-step5-review.stderr.$$`). Check whether these files are cleaned up on all exit paths, whether they are properly confined to IMPLEMENT_TMPDIR, and whether the `set +e` / `set -e` bracketing is safe in the context of the outer script's error-handling contract. Examine whether `awk` parsing of the captured stdout for STEP5_REVIEW_STATUS can silently produce the wrong case-match value, causing the wrong ledger path to execute. Also inspect the new `_RCC_LAST_FAILURE_CAPTURE_PATH` and `_RCC_LAST_LEDGER_FAILURE_DETAIL_LOG` accumulators in ship-pr.sh for reset-before-use correctness across multiple iterations of the fix loop. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
